en: The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the Wrathful Vidyārāja Trailokyavijaya,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of Daxingshan Temple, the Great Sage of Broad Wisdom,
who was promoted to the rank of Acting Court Gentleman for Foreigners.
Translated by Amoghavajra by imperial decree: At that time, all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and holy sages appeared in the world to benefit all sentient beings;
yet the times were such that they did not accord with the characteristics of the True Dharma.
Because the great and profound vows of Akṣobhya Samantabhadra are so vast, he manifests in a wrathful form to subdue those who harm the lands, sentient beings, and Māras.
He addressed the Buddha, saying:
I am within the mantra;
it is extremely rare in the world that the Tathāgatas have been permitted to proclaim this mantra.
"We shall protect the Buddha's teachings and benefit all sentient beings.
At that time, the Buddha said:
"Excellent, excellent, O Wrathful King!"
Listen as I recite the mantra for subduing.
At that moment, he manifested the form of an extremely fierce and great wrathful deity with four faces and eight arms,
and spoke these verses of the mantra syllables.
The mantra is:
Oṃ susū hūṃ phaṭ svāhā hūṃ | Gṛhṇa gṛhṇa hūṃ | Gṛhṇāpaya hūṃ ānaya hūṃ bhagavan vajra hūṃ phaṭ ṭhaḥ | At that time, the Great Being Samantabhadra and the others...
When this mantra was spoken,
the trichiliocosm shook in six ways,
and all the realms of devas and māras were shaken.
Those who cause harm to sentient beings were all struck with terror and found no peace;
they fled in all directions and gathered before the Wrathful Lord, addressing him thus:
"I only pray that you will take pity on me and grant me freedom from fear.
At that time, the Wrathful King caused all to attain peace and security.
Then, with his right foot he treads upon the Māra King Mahāśvara,
and with his left foot he treads upon the Māra Queen;
[he acts thus] for the sake of sentient beings within the realm.
May all be made to attain happiness.
By reciting this mantra once,
the immeasurable and boundless realms of Māra [are subdued].
Because they are each afflicted by the fever of suffering,
those who create obstacles for the practitioner find no opportunity; instead,
they become the practitioner’s servants and even go so far as to cause hindrances.
The practitioner should properly protect the three karmas both internally and externally.
This may also involve performing the ritual procedures for the mudrās that expel obstructors and bind the boundaries, as well as sealing the five locations of the body.
It can be seen that within the Vajraśekhara Yoga teachings,
there is no further need for translation,
nor is it necessary to perform various ritual mudrās.
However, all powers and verifications reside in this mantra;
there is no other separate incantation.
One who wishes to practice this mantra should face east.
One sits before the image in a wrathful posture.
Visualizing one's own body as no different from the majestic and wrathful King of the Honored One (Bhagavān),
one thereby purifies the three karmas.
Regarding the so-called three recitations of the syllable *HŪṂ*:
one likewise establishes the Dharma-realm by forming the firm vajra-bind with both hands and placing them upon the forehead.
Turning three times to the left and right also accomplishes the expulsion of obstructors and the demarcation of the boundary.
Next, join your palms at the heart and prostrate to the wrathful deities and the assembly of noble ones.
If one wishes to subjugate all evil persons,
construct a triangular hearth with the altar facing south.
Take wood from a malevolent tree and burn it once for each repetition,
until three hundred and twenty-four repetitions are complete.
The evil person will spontaneously submit and develop faith and refuge.
Furthermore, if one wishes to subdue evil persons or those afflicted by illness,
one should construct a *tāḍana-maṇḍala* and recite the root mantra one thousand and eighty times.
Burn two types of mustard seeds— red and black—
burning one thousand and eighty grains for each round.
Recite the person's name within the mantra phrases as you do so.
Thus, one washes away chronic illness and attains freedom from death.
If one wishes to eliminate disease,
one should perform the *śāntika* (pacifying) altar facing east.
Burn one thousand grains of white rice, chanting the mantra once for each grain.
If the word "removal of illness" (*vyādhi-nirghāta*) is inserted within the mantra, illnesses will be pacified,
and [the beings] will take refuge in the Buddha-dharma.
One must not harbor a distracted mind, just as one would with this wooden branch.
If one wishes to suddenly extinguish an evil person,
one should place that person's name and image within the fire-pit.
If one recites the mantra one hundred and eight times with a malicious mind,
and strikes an evil person with sand while burning it,
that person will die.
If one wishes for an urgent recovery,
one should recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times before the Wrathful King with a mind of compassion.
However, they will not be harmed and will recover without injury.
If one wishes to be victorious in battle,
one should take one hundred and eight pieces of fragrant wood.
Recite the mantra while burning [the offerings];
thus, even against an army of demonic enemies, one will immediately achieve victory.
One must also include the five grains and the five fragrances.
If it is not available, wherever you may be,
do not be distressed by its absence.
If you wish to enter mountain forests, you shall not encounter evil birds, beasts, or venomous insects.
Hold a pebble within the palms of both hands and recite the mantra twenty-one times;
strike it forward upon the path,
and even birds, beasts, and venomous insects will all be subdued.
May there be no harm or injury to the mind.
If one wishes to be revered and loved by kings and ministers,
construct a mandala for the rite of reverence and burn one hundred and eight roots of chrysanthemum.
Recite the mantra once and burn [the substance] once; then, one will naturally be the object of others' respect and affection.
If you wish to assist those who are gravely ill, recite the mantra over scented water one hundred and eight times before an image.
If one quickly inserts it into the patient's abdomen,
they will awaken.
If one wishes to retain the epilepsy or chronic illness [in the body], [one should act accordingly].
If one takes dragon water and recites the mantra one hundred and eight times over it,
washing the two eyes, mouth, tongue, and so forth,
[the afflictions] will naturally be extinguished and no other diseases will remain.
If one wishes to bind a man or a woman so that they speak only a single word,
take a branch of *dāḍima* wood one zhang two chi long, empower it ten thousand times with mantras,
and then place it in another location.
Recite the mantra once for each strike with a branch.
Strike the person at twenty-eight locations;
immediately, all matters will be revealed through speech in response to whatever is asked.
One should then imagine and mentally conceive oneself as being released from bondage.
If a practitioner cultivates this dharma for a period of seven times seven days, [the result will follow].
One must sever attachment to the flavors of the five grains and salt, and with single-minded focus on no other object, recite the mantra one hundred thousand times.
At that time, the Honored One will manifest his form,
assuming a body of great and terrifying majesty to subdue Māra.
One should test the mind of the practitioner of humility;
at that time, one must be careful not to give rise to distraction, for then the dharma will be accomplished.
At that moment, the Wrathful King spoke this mantra.
All celestial Māras, evil spirits,
and the like were all thoroughly subdued;
they then believed and accepted the Buddha-way, taking refuge in it.
Each practitioner, acting as a guardian,
next dissolves the boundary and bows to the Buddha before leaving the hall.
Read sūtras such as the *Prajñāpāramitā* at will.
The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the Wrathful Vidyārāja Trailokyavijaya.
